newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK SAYS APV MAY HAGGLE OVER PAY-OUT.
newsitem.headline: TVK SAYS APV MAY HAGGLE OVER PAY-OUT.

text.p: Chemicals company Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat (TVK) officials said on Thursday their request for five billion forints request submitted to the state privatisation agency APV Rt may be subject to negotiation.
"Some sort of bargain (with APV) is imaginable," Miklos Varhegyi, TKV's president CEO, told a news conference.
The amount stems from the company's privatisation and is based on Hungary's 1989 privatisation law, he added.
Varhegyi said he did not know what TVK's chances were for actually receiving the full amount.
"Whatever our chances, we could not let this opportunity slip," he said.
He added that the possibility of claiming 20 percent of the privatisation income arose following an APV board decision in November.
Varhegyi said that other companies could follow TVK's move.

CS First Boston's Budapest-based analyst Spencer Jakab said in a company update that if the cash transfer is approved, it would raise TVK's earnings per share to 527 forints from the previously expected 477 forints.
"We reiterate our enthusisastic 'buy' recommendation on TVK with or without the benefit of the cash transfer," Jakab said. "The stock remains our top pick on the Hungarian market."
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, TVK shares stood at 1,840 forints, up 10 at 1143 GMT.
